title: Preconditioned DeltaNet: Curvature-aware Sequence Modeling for Linear Recurrences

claims.text: Theorem 3.1 establishes that the Preconditioned DeltaNet (PDN) recursion satisfies S_t = C_t P_t for all t, formally deriving the equivalence between linear attention and the delta rule under exact preconditioning (Section 3.1, Theorem 3.1).

A diagonal approximation to the key Gram matrix (Eq. 7) enables efficient preconditioned variants of DeltaNet, GDN, and KDA with chunkwise-parallel algorithms, incurring only about 10% throughput overhead relative to the base models (Section 3.3, Figure 3).
At 340M parameters on SlimPajama, PGDN attains average zero-shot commonsense accuracy of 49.96% versus 48.86% for GDN, and average in-context recall accuracy of 26.17% versus 24.77% (Table 1).
At 1B parameters, PGDN attains average zero-shot commonsense accuracy of 56.38% versus 55.44% for GDN, and average in-context recall accuracy of 34.99% versus 33.87% (Table 1).

PGDN maintains or improves performance over baselines on the MQAR synthetic multi-query associative recall benchmark across varying sequence lengths, and shows improvements on the S-NIAH benchmark (Figures 5 and 6).
